hypothesis: Fusing absolute value into the grid-stride reduction avoids the scratch write/read and one kernel launch. A grid of ceil(n/256), capped at 1024 CTAs, avoids needless atomics for small inputs while bounding CTA-level atomics for large inputs. Whether those savings offset the required output reset and atomic contention must be measured; the controller must validate FP64 tolerance for every required size and seed.
notes: The reset and reduction kernel are both issued on the default stream, preserving per-call output initialization without scratch state. The supplied baseline is correct at 1.228 ms mean; no hierarchical candidate measurements are present here. Compare complete timings including reset and launch overhead against those candidates; no performance or correctness result is claimed for this proposal.
transformations: Fuse fabsf(input) into the per-thread grid-stride accumulation, eliminating the intermediate scratch array and its producer kernel.
Retain an asynchronous per-call output reset in the default stream before reduction.
Set CTA count to ceil(n/256), capped at 1024, and perform one output atomicAdd per CTA.
